--- title: "Get started" jupyter: php --- ## Install the kernel A kernelspec belongs to the machine, so the usual choice is to install juphyter once for your user, as [Installation](install.qmd) describes. Installing it as a development dependency of one project pins the kernel's version with that project, at the cost of a kernelspec that names that project's copy of the engine: ```bash composer require --dev phpstats/juphyter vendor/bin/juphyter install ``` The command prints what the kernel is made of. ``` Installed the juphyter kernel "php" for PHP 8.5.10. kernel.json /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php/kernel.json python /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (ipykernel 7.4.0) php /opt/homebrew/bin/php engine /path/to/vendor/phpstats/juphyter/bin/juphyter quarto /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (jupyter_client 8.10.0) ``` The Python is the interpreter that owns the `jupyter` on `PATH`, because the kernel runs inside it. `--python` names a different one. The PHP is the binary that runs the cells, and `--php` names a different one, which is how several versions coexist: ```bash vendor/bin/juphyter install --name php83 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.3/bin/php vendor/bin/juphyter install --name php85 --php /opt/homebrew/opt/php@8.5/bin/php ``` `juphyter uninstall --name php83` removes a kernelspec juphyter wrote, and refuses to remove one it did not. The `quarto` line appears when Quarto is installed. Quarto runs an interpreter of its own choosing, and that one is the one that needs Jupyter in it, so the line reports which interpreter that is and what was found there. When it says `(no Jupyter)`, the kernelspec is still correct and `quarto render` cannot reach it; [Installation](install.qmd) covers the fix. On a machine with no Python that can host the kernel at all, the command offers to build one. [Installation](install.qmd) covers that and the `--create-venv` option that answers the offer in advance. ## A first cell A cell is PHP without an opening tag. The value of the last expression is the cell's result, and `echo` goes to the cell's output stream. ::: {#72b9f2ff .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.php .cell-code} $primes = [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13]; echo count($primes), " primes, summing to ", array_sum($primes), "\n"; array_sum($primes) / count($primes); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 6 primes, summing to 41 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 6.833333333333333 ``` ::: ::: State carries between cells, so the next cell sees what this one bound. ::: {#537f7da3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.php .cell-code} $primes[] = 17; $primes; ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17] ``` ::: ::: ## Imports A `use` statement applies to the cells after it as well as to its own. The session accumulates them, so a notebook can put its imports in a first cell and use short class names from then on. ::: {#af058688 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.php .cell-code} use DateTimeImmutable; $released = new DateTimeImmutable('2026-11-20'); $released->format('F Y'); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 3, line 0 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'November 2026' ``` ::: ::: `namespace` is not supported in a cell, and a cell cannot redeclare a class or a function that another cell already declared. PHP has no way to undefine either, so a second run of a cell that declares one reports what it would have redeclared rather than failing in the middle. ## Errors A cell that throws reports the exception, its message, and the stack frames that raised it, with each stack frame naming the cell and the line rather than `eval()'d code`. ::: {#afbcc435 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.php .cell-code} $widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12]; $mean = fn (array $values) => array_sum($values) / count($values); $mean([]); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 4, line 0 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-error} ``` DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero in a closure at Cell 4, line 5 ``` ::: ::: Warnings, notices, and deprecations go to the cell's error stream and leave the cell running. ::: {#ba7398d8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.php .cell-code} $widths = ['narrow' => 4, 'wide' => 12]; $widths['narrow'] + $widths['medium']; ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 5, line 0 Warning: Undefined array key "medium" in Cell 5, line 3 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: ## Rich display A value is published in every representation the front end might draw. A phibble data frame comes with an HTML table and the tibble-style text phibble prints at a terminal, and a phiz plot comes with a Vega-Lite specification, an HTML embed, a static SVG when vl-convert is installed, and a one-line description. ::: {#548132d9 .cell execution_count=6} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 6, line -1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#0121711c .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.php .cell-code} DataFrame::fromRows([ ['package' => 'phibble', 'purpose' => 'data frames', 'version' => 0.3], ['package' => 'phplyr', 'purpose' => 'dplyr verbs', 'version' => 0.3], ['package' => 'phiz', 'purpose' => 'plots', 'version' => 0.3], ]); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 7, line -1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7} ```{=html}
A tibble: 3 × 3
package <chr>purpose <chr>version <dbl>
1phibbledata frames0.3
2phplyrdplyr verbs0.3
3phizplots0.3
``` ::: ::: Any class can opt in. A `toHtml(): string` method supplies the `text/html` representation, and a `toMimeBundle(): array` method supplies the whole bundle. ::: {#07ba6a9f .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.php .cell-code} final class Progress { public function __construct(private readonly int $done, private readonly int $total) {} public function toHtml(): string { return sprintf( ' %d of %d', $this->done, $this->total, $this->done, $this->total, ); } public function __toString(): string { return sprintf('%d of %d', $this->done, $this->total); } } new Progress(7, 9); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 8, line -1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ```{=html} 7 of 9 ``` ::: ::: `Juphyter\display()` publishes a value part way through a cell, so one cell can show several data frames or plots. ::: {#42b80c5d .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.php .cell-code} Juphyter\display(new Progress(3, 9)); Juphyter\display(new Progress(9, 9)); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning: The use statement with non-compound name 'DateTimeImmutable' has no effect in Cell 9, line -1 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html} 3 of 9 ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html} 9 of 9 ``` ::: ::: ## Where to go next [Quarto](quarto.qmd) covers rendering a `.qmd` to HTML, `ipynb`, and PDF. [JupyterLab](jupyter.qmd) covers the notebook interface and what it draws.
